scope: Isolated S1 script-thread failures after response headers. One case fails an active document before Servo creates its DOM. The other fails an active document whose parser waits for a withheld script. No engine, product dependency, or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: Patch servo-net so request interception cannot replace a crash error page (2026-11-26).
An error page is recoverable by navigating back, reloading, or editing the target URL (2026-11-24).

baseline.head: 7affa0a
baseline.note: The crash history evidence records three passing runs in each mode at this checkpoint. origin/main was at b2cacaf when this work started.

configuration.crash_page_check: Each fetched crash document must contain the engine's failure reason. Servo's crash.html embeds that reason. The check only orders the fixture and grants no host authority.
configuration.partial_response_check: Servo's request interceptor buffers an intercepted body until the load finishes, so the partial responses come from a loopback HTTP server through the real loader. The withheld parser script uses interception, which never answers until release. Fixture markers and page state only order the fixture and grant no host authority.

changes.name: Failure before the DOM exists
changes.observed: Servo activates a navigation's document when response headers arrive. Its parser buffers the first 1,445 body bytes for MIME sniffing before it creates the DOM. Until then the active document has no document element and has run no script.
changes.fix: None. A new case holds a shorter body open in that state, unwinds the script thread, and checks revocation, callback release, the crash page, late data, reload, and a new URL.

changes.name: Failure while the parser is blocked
changes.observed: With a body longer than the sniffing buffer, the parser runs an inline script and blocks on a classic script. Servo's prefetch tokenizer and the parser each request that script, so the host withholds two requests.
changes.fix: None. A new case unwinds the script thread in that state and runs the same checks.

changes.name: Stale summary case count
changes.observed: The crash history commit added a case but left the summary marker at 41 and 51 cases. The runner accepted it because it checked only the summary name.
changes.fix: The summary now reports 44 and 54 cases. The runner requires the summary count to equal the number of expected case markers, and a runner test covers a stale count.

findings: Both failures revoke host scope before eight terminal callbacks in both modes. The failed identity becomes stale, and the crash page shows the failure reason.

After the failure, the host releases the withheld scripts and the rest of the main body. The crash page keeps its identity, no other failure occurs, and the engine reports no error. The failed document never reports DOM readiness or load completion.
The loopback server's write of the held tail succeeded in every run. This shows only that the socket accepted the bytes, not whether Servo read them.
Reload from the crash page restores the failed URL with its loopback origin. A new URL also recovers.

single_process.scope: Experimental engine scope, host allocation gate, script-thread unwind, final-handle release, explicit engine shutdown, queued execution cancellation, interruption of running JavaScript, content-process exit and forced kill in multiprocess mode, shared-process view revocation and ordinary sibling close, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill before document construction, crash recovery through reload and history, callback and delegate unwind safety, and constellation loss in a separate engine. Remaining replacement audits remain open.
